name: AI Energy Boom
description: Hypothesis scenario: no effective demand cap on energy — AI compute and robotics have near-unbounded appetite. Levers vs baseline (endogenous-rule era): AI cognitive labor payoff on (aiWorkerEquivalentPerTWh 1e5), low robot integration friction (robotIntegrationExponent 0.5, diffusion 0.30), and a datacenter power-spend ceiling 10x baseline (0.5% of GDP). COMPOSITE-DC-CAPEX RESCORE (July 2026): chips and facilities are charged together at the default $15B per average GW with 15% annual replacement. DC capex rises from ~$0.28T in 2025 to ~$0.68T in 2030, ~$23.5T in 2050, ~$57.1T in 2075, and ~$130.6T in 2100. Competition for the shared investment pool self-brakes the prior path: the funding-floor violation disappears, but WACC still reaches ~15.2% in 2075 and ~22.1% in 2100. Outputs reach GDP ~$3,956T, generation ~2.74M TWh, robots ~34,000/1000 workers, datacenters ~508k TWh, and warming ~2.89C in 2100. Treat this highly path-dependent upper envelope as a stress test, not a forecast; DC capacity rationing and dedicated lease/debt service remain unmodeled.
